decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm approach to the set square, gradually pitching the open gripper downward while preserving a continuous elbow-up posture.
Continue open-gripper approach above the right portion of the ruler; rotate toward a vertical grasp with jaws across its narrow dimension.
Move toward the ruler's right-side grasp point while continuing the smooth downward orientation change.
Finish approaching above the right-hand segment of the ruler, correcting the downward grasp orientation before lowering to contact.
Bring the gripper vertically above the ruler near its right end. Hold sufficient height to avoid scraping the table before assessing fingertip alignment.
Center the downward fingers across the ruler and lower cautiously. Partially close to inspect engagement, without approaching any cube.
Close on the set square and make a small table-parallel test slide toward the cubes. Check visible ruler motion rather than relying on gripper state.
Slide the gripped straightedge toward the blocks at constant height, using its long edge to gather their near faces into one line.
Relieve a few millimeters of possible tabletop pressure while keeping the straightedge low. Inspect whether the tool is securely retained before a longer push.
The ruler's left end appears to lag. Bring the left arm toward that end for support while the right holds still; keep each arm in its own workspace.
Continue the left-side support approach above the ruler's end, with the right grip stationary and all cubes untouched.
Advance the left gripper above the tool's left section while continuing its smooth vertical reorientation; do not contact the nearby cubes.
Position the left open jaws around the tool's left section; maintain clearance and the right-hand hold.
Complete the left vertical approach over the end of the straightedge, then inspect jaw placement before closing.
Lower the left jaws slightly and close around the ruler away from all blocks. Establish support at both ends before the planar alignment push.
Test a coordinated low slide with both ends supported, advancing the lagging left end slightly more. Watch the straightedge and cubes for actual planar movement.
Advance both grips together, keeping the straightedge low and its orientation fixed so all three cube faces meet the same long edge.
All three blocks now visibly meet the straightedge. Use a final short, slow planar seating push, then pause before separating the tool.
Withdraw the straightedge a short distance parallel to the tabletop, leaving the aligned blocks in place and keeping both grips away from them.
Release the straightedge onto the table and lift only the empty grippers clear. The cubes remain ungrasped; begin resetting both arms.
Retract both empty grippers upward and toward the robot while smoothly undoing the grasp orientation. Leave the aligned row and ruler untouched.
Continue a smooth, separate-workspace return toward the recorded starting poses, with open empty grippers and elbow-up continuity.
Continue returning both empty arms to their original positions and orientations without disturbing the straight aligned row.
Continue the controlled reset along the same elbow-up branches, with both grippers open and clear of the table objects.
Approach the home poses gradually, maintaining configuration continuity and leaving the tabletop alignment undisturbed.
Slow the final approach to the recorded home poses to respect joint-continuity limits near the starting configuration.
